problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.4 & 0.6 & 0.9 \\ 0.4 & 0.2 & 0 \\ 0.2 & 0.2 & 0.1\end{aligned}],\,q=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $q$ is the steady-state vector of the stochastic matrix $P$ shown above, what is the value of $a+b-c?$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Steady-State Vector of a Stochastic 3x3 Matrix
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14061943/assets/093de94431946cb83e7cc0523405989b7a23cc8d9677bdecdfba7aaf207fd62b.png)

Find the steady-state vector $\mathbf q$ of the stochastic matrix $P$ shown above.
examples.worked_solution:
Recall that a steady-state vector of a stochastic matrix $P$ is a stochastic vector $\mathbf{q}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}Pq & =q \\ Pq-q & =0 \\ Pq-Iq & =0 \\ (P-I)q & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $P-I,$ we get

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14061943/assets/5ed2f76d9b2857134a5b2aa5781711f9625cabb46a9ca3c3d54aa31c32bb4dbe.png)

The matrix equation $(P-I)\mathbf{q} = \mathbf{0}$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-0.9 & 0.3 & 0.5 & 0 \\ 0.2 & -0.7 & 0.1 & 0 \\ 0.7 & 0.4 & -0.6 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=20{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2}:=10{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:=20{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-18 & 6 & 10 & 0 \\ 2 & -7 & 1 & 0 \\ 14 & 8 & -12 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}↔{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -7 & 1 & 0 \\ -18 & 6 & 10 & 0 \\ 14 & 8 & -12 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+9{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-7{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -7 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -57 & 19 & 0 \\ 0 & 57 & -19 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -7 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -57 & 19 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, $x_3$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain 

$$
x_2=\dfrac{1}{3}x_3.
$$

 
Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
2x_1 -7\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x_3\right) + x_3 = 0 \qquad \Longrightarrow\qquad x_1 = \dfrac{2}{3}x_3.
$$

Hence, the general solution is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14061943/assets/9ae5533dc825d2d3d08ca7a54c50578e21dda8fad7988b9043baaad2a69368b7.png)

Since the steady-state vector must be stochastic, its entries should add up to $1.$ Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3}+\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3}+{x}_{3} & =1 \\ 2{x}_{3} & =1 \\ {x}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, our steady-state vector is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14061943/assets/fd7775b5d982d0bc51e80417a70b67dbff0176afcc5ff9aec613947076201386.png)

feedback.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.35 & 1 \\ 0.65 & 0\end{aligned}],\,q=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $q$ is the steady-state vector of the stochastic matrix $P,$ what is the value of $a-b?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that a steady-state vector of a stochastic matrix $P$ is a stochastic vector $q$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}Pq & =q \\ Pq-q & =0 \\ Pq-Iq & =0 \\ (P-I)q & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $P-I,$ we get

$$
P-I=[\begin{aligned}0.35 & 1 \\ 0.65 & 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-0.65 & 1 \\ 0.65 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

The matrix equation $(P-I)q=0$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-0.65 & 1 & 0 \\ 0.65 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-0.65 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}-0.65{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =0 \\ 65{x}_{1}-100{x}_{2} & =0 \\ 13{x}_{1}-20{x}_{2} & =0 \\ {x}_{1} & =\frac{20}{13}{x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{20}{13}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Since the steady-state vector must be stochastic, its entries should add up to $1.$ Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{20}{13}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2} & =1 \\ \frac{33}{13}{x}_{2} & =1 \\ {x}_{2} & =\frac{13}{33}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
q=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{20}{33} \\ \frac{13}{33}\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a-b=\frac{20}{33}-\frac{13}{33}=\frac{7}{33}.$
